issues.finding: No invariant test asserts that every registered route is auth-gated, and no such property is checkable from the current test structure (see S03). The scan behind S01/S02/S06/S07 was a regex over .route(...) registrations matching 68 of 153 registrations repo-wide (routes/api.rs yielded 26 of its 53). The remaining ~85 registrations were checked by no method at all. More unauthenticated routes may exist; this manifest does not claim to have found them all. UPDATE 2026-09-06 (revision 3): the sweep now EXISTS on branch remediation/web-auth (commit d46d2a9), inventories 166 route registrations (55 always-compiled + 111 creator-only) and asserts 401-for-bogus-key against an explicit public allowlist. Reviewer ran it. It is only PARTIALLY effective: 49 registrations (13 always + 36 creator) return 422/400 because axum's body extractors reject a malformed body BEFORE the handler's auth check runs, so the sweep marks them 'inconclusive' rather than passing them. Those 49 are proven neither gated nor ungated by any method. UPDATE 2026-09-06 (revision 6), branch remediation/auth-sweep: FIXED (commit cac829b): ALLOWLIST renamed KNOWN_PUBLIC; both sweeps now hard-ASSERT on inconclusive as well as on violations, where inconclusive was previously only eprintln'd and silently absorbed. Reviewer's mutation test confirms the assertions fire.
issues.remediation_and_acceptance: Send a schema-valid body for each mutating route so the request reaches the handler and the auth check actually runs, converting all 49 inconclusive results into real assertions. Then resolve the red-branch problem: the two sweeps currently FAIL by design because they found real gaps (S13/S14/S15), and CI gates on `cargo test --workspace`. Do NOT #[ignore] them — that is skip laundering. Convert to an exact-match assertion against a declared known-unauthenticated list, so the suite is green, every listed gap is visible, and any NEW ungated route fails the build. Acceptance: zero inconclusive results, and the known-gap list is empty. REVIEWER NOTE on the guard's limits: the sweep asserts COMPOSED behaviour, so wrongly adding a route to KNOWN_PUBLIC is NOT caught when that route's handler still performs its own check_key/check_dual (verified by mutation: allowlisting /api/v1/channels kept the sweep green because the handler rejected the request anyway). That is defense in depth working, not a hole — but it means the sweep guards the middleware, not the allowlist. An allowlist error on a route WITHOUT a handler check is caught.
